hero.headline: Open arts for AI agents
hero.sub_copy: MIT-licensed registry of skills + a multi-model review CLI. Compose pipelines once; run them on Claude, Codex, Gemini, DeepSeek — or any provider you add to agents.yaml.
tagline_lines: Agent-first: your AI coding agent installs and runs jutsu.
Local-first. No telemetry. No registry lock-in.

failure_demo.intro: Single-agent review is sycophancy by default. Same prompt, same model, run twice — you usually get the same "LGTM." Adversarial review needs structural disagreement, not rerolls.
failure_demo.outro: kaijutsu fans the same diff across multiple models, shows where they agree, and flags exactly where they don't. The disagreement table is the artifact you read.
failure_demo.left_body: “LGTM. Clean rename, well-scoped. Tests look comprehensive.”

quickstart.intro: kaijutsu is agent-first: jutsu is meant to be invoked BY your AI coding agent on your behalf. The first time, point your agent at kaijutsu.dev — after that, jutsu init writes a fragment into AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md so future agent sessions already know what the tool is.
quickstart.step1_intro: Paste the kaijutsu URL to your coding agent (Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI), or run the install yourself. Either way, jutsu init drops the persistent context fragment.
quickstart.user_says: Set up kaijutsu from https://kaijutsu.dev in this repo. Run jutsu init. Then install the pr-review skill. Tell me which API keys I still need to export.
quickstart.snippet_install:
curl -fsSL https://kaijutsu.dev/install.sh | sh
jutsu init                              # detects active agents, writes .kaijutsu/ + AGENTS.md fragment
jutsu install pr-review                 # add the pr-review skill
jutsu agent doctor                      # verify provider env vars + reachability
quickstart.step2_intro: Future agent sessions read the AGENTS.md fragment and already know what jutsu does — no URL re-paste needed.
quickstart.user_says_2: Run a multi-agent pr-review on my current branch and post as a PR comment.
quickstart.snippet_output:
claude     │ ✓ │ ✗ │ ✓
gemini     │ ✓ │ ✓ │ ✗
deepseek   │ ✗ │ ✓ │ ✓

           severity   file:line                summary
           issue      auth.go:42               token expiry uses < not <=

quickstart.manual_note: Prefer to type it yourself? Every command above works in a normal terminal — jutsu doesn't care who's typing.

portability.intro: Write a swarm.yaml once. jutsu dispatches it across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, DeepSeek-via-HTTP, and whatever vendor ships next. v0.6's driver abstraction handles the wire format per vendor; v0.13's Preset SDK lets you compose your own pipelines. Vendor lock-in stays a vendor problem.
portability.snippet_yaml:
# .kaijutsu/swarm.yaml — composable, portable, version-controlled
version: 1
presets:
  - name: tight-pr-review
    base: pr-review
    personas:
      - default-claude
      - paranoid-security-claude
      - default-gemini
    mode: full
    confidence_floor: 0.7
portability.callout_body: Vendor IDEs will ship native multi-agent review by 2027. Cross-vendor portability is the part that doesn't commodify. Your pipeline is yours, regardless of which vendor wins.

cost.intro: Multi-agent review costs more per call than a single-agent run. The framing that matters is cost per bug actually caught and confirmed real, not cost per call.
cost.table_caption: Receipt from a real run. Reproducible: same prompt + same providers + cold cache should land within ±20% (vendor pricing drifts; rate limits / context refresh affect timing).

rows.value: doc-review on the v0.14 landing-page content spec

cost.objection_body: Yes — that's what you're buying. Three models with different priors disagree about different things. The cost difference is the disagreement. If your codebase doesn't need disagreement, run jutsu swarm pr-review with --personas default-claude only.

parts.title: MIT-licensed, end to end
parts.body: kaijutsu CLI, every core skill, the registry index — all MIT. No CLA, no rug-pull license clause, no "open core" tier. Fork it. The LICENSE file in every skill is part of the integrity check.

parts.title: Skill provenance
parts.body: Core skills (skills/core/*) are sigstore-signed at release. jutsu install verifies the signature before unpacking. Community skills are pinned to a tagged commit + SHA + sha256 integrity in kaijutsu.lock.json; tampering breaks the lockfile.

parts.title: Permission gates + supply-chain
parts.body: Skills can request bash, network, fs-write. jutsu install parses each skill's permissions: manifest before write and prompts on first sensitive use. Skills are arbitrary code that runs in your agent loop — pin to SHA, audit the diff, do not auto-update.

parts.title: Local data stays local
parts.body: ~/.kaijutsu/findings.db is mode 0600, never leaves disk, never syncs. The cli/internal/cli/finding.go package is import-list-restricted from net, net/http, net/url — enforced as a build-time test.

parts.title: Receipts, not rhetoric
parts.body: Every kaijutsu release links to the actual jutsu swarm pr-review that reviewed it. Self-review is necessary, not sufficient — but it's a falsifiable receipt, not a marketing badge.

trust.wrapper_title: Isn't this just a wrapper around OpenAI/Anthropic APIs?
trust.wrapper_intro: The honest answer: it has wrapper parts and non-wrapper parts.
trust.wrapper_inside: Per-vendor driver shims (cli/http/cli-compat/mcp). Intentionally thin — vendor APIs change, and we want the change surface small.
wrapper_outside: Cross-vendor portability layer — same swarm.yaml runs across vendors with different wire formats and auth.

findings.db quality fingerprinting — per-(provider, persona, preset, codebase) precision math derived from your accept/dismiss history. The synthesizer weights each agent's vote by observed precision. No vendor offers this.
Preset SDK — compose your own swarm shapes; project + home overlay; built-ins shadowed at registration.
Dream lens-blindspot warnings — jutsu swarm dream --mode full --lenses all runs the 8-lens matrix and flags where lens consensus may be RLHF-convergence rather than actual signal.
agents.yaml driver abstraction — provider catalog with overlay + override semantics; vendor switch is a config edit.

contributing.intro: Skills + tools live at github.com/momentmaker/kaijutsu. Read CONTRIBUTING.md for skill authoring + PR conventions.
contributing.body: Want to add a skill? jutsu skill new <name> scaffolds a flat-layout skill directory. jutsu lint <path> validates schema + license + permission manifest. Run jutsu publish to open a PR against skills/community/.
